h1: A career in beer marketing and brand management
title: A Career in Beer Marketing and Brands | Craft Beer School
desc: What beer marketing and brand management jobs involve in India, the skills they need, how alcohol ad rules shape the work and how to get in.
teaser: In most industries, brand managers can buy a TV advert. In Indian beer, they mostly cannot. That changes the whole job.
standfirst: Beer marketing looks glamorous from outside: launches, events, design. The real work is analysis, planning and working within tight rules. We look at the roles, skills and routes into beer marketing and brand management in India.
sections:
A beer marketing team decides how a brand is positioned, who it is for, how it looks and how it reaches drinkers. In a large brewer, that work is spread across several roles. In a craft brewery, one or two people may do all of it.

The main jobs are understanding drinkers, shaping the brand, planning launches and campaigns and working with sales on what happens in bars and shops. Then they measure whether any of it worked. Our guide to beer brand portfolios explains how brands sit together in a company.

• Brand manager. Owns one or more brands: positioning, plans, budgets and results.
  • Trade marketing. Works on what happens in shops, bars and restaurants: displays, menus, promotions and staff training.
  • Activation or experiential marketing. Runs events, sponsorships and tastings.
  • Consumer insights. Studies drinkers through research and data.
  • Digital marketing. Social media, websites and online content.
  • Innovation. Develops new beers and pack formats with brewing teams.

Large companies have specialists in each. In craft breweries, the marketing lead often covers most of them and works closely with the founders.
Why Indian rules change the job

Alcohol advertising in India is tightly restricted. Direct advertising of alcohol in many media is not allowed. Rules on promotion also vary by state. This shapes beer marketing more than almost anything else.

Because of this, beer marketers in India put more effort into trade marketing, events, packaging, digital content within platform rules and partnerships. The bar, the shop shelf and the experience become the main media. Understanding these rules is part of the job. Good marketers work closely with legal and compliance teams.

• Understanding the product. Knowing beer styles, how beer is made and what drinkers taste. Our guide to beer styles for marketing teams is a good start.
  • Analysis. Reading sales data, share figures and research to decide what to do.
  • Planning and budgets. Building plans and spending money where it works.
  • Creative judgement. Briefing agencies and designers and knowing good work when you see it.
  • Working with sales. Marketing that does not help sales teams sell is wasted.
  • Compliance awareness. Knowing what can and cannot be said and shown.

People who understand both the beer and the numbers stand out. Many marketing people know branding but cannot talk confidently about the liquid. That shows in meetings with brewers.

Common entry routes include:

  • Management trainee programmes at large brewers and drinks companies, often for MBA graduates.
  • Moving from marketing roles in other consumer goods, such as food, soft drinks or personal care.
  • Joining an agency that works on beer brands, then moving client side.
  • Starting in sales or trade marketing and moving into brand roles. Our guide to brewery sales careers covers that path.
  • Joining a craft brewery in a small, broad role and growing with it.

Craft breweries often value hands-on experience and a genuine interest in beer over formal titles. Large companies tend to look for structured experience and qualifications.
Building your knowledge before you apply

Learn about beer itself. Taste widely, understand styles and visit breweries. Learn how brands are built: positioning, personas and brand voice. Follow how Indian beer brands present themselves within the rules and think about why they make the choices they do.

Spend time in the trade as well. Talk to bartenders about which beers move and why. Watch how people choose in a liquor shop. These observations make you far more useful in a brand meeting than theory alone.

A small portfolio helps, especially for craft brewery roles: a brand analysis, a mock launch plan for a beer or social content you have made. It shows how you think, which matters more than a long list of courses.

Brand managers can move up to senior brand roles, category leadership and marketing director positions. Some move into general management or start their own brands. Others become consultants or join agencies. The skills also transfer across drinks categories, from beer to spirits, wine and non-alcoholic drinks.

Wherever you aim, the core skill is the same: understanding a drinker deeply enough to give them a reason to choose your beer.
faqs: Do I need an MBA for beer marketing?
Large brewers often hire MBA graduates for trainee roles, but many people enter from sales, agencies or other consumer goods. Craft breweries care more about practical skills and interest in beer.
How do Indian alcohol ad rules affect beer marketing?
Direct advertising is restricted in many media, so marketers focus on trade marketing, events, packaging and compliant digital content. Rules vary by state.
Do beer marketers need to know brewing?
Not in depth, but knowing styles and how beer is made helps you talk to brewers and drinkers credibly.
